meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/03, Monday 10 June 2024). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: June 2024 series, despite the download folder's Nov 24 label — this paper is dated Monday 10 June 2024. No per-question total is printed, so the whole-paper sum against the published 100 is the only check, and this file passes it. Coded WITH mark_split, derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes rather than quoted.

coding_notes: q17 (simple interest, then the total value) tagged percentage_change and NOT growth_and_decay, following the documented ruling on OCR-JUN25-F-P1 q22: growth_and_decay is compound, and simple interest demonstrates nothing about a repeated multiplier.

q19 (two reasons a graph is misleading) tagged simple_charts, the documented handling for misleading graphs, rather than time_series — the faults the mark scheme wants are an uneven horizontal scale, a missing vertical scale and a vertical scale not starting at zero, which are chart-reading points, not trend points.

q13b (smallest possible number of newspapers) tagged lowest_common_multiple first: the answer is 200 because it must satisfy both a percentage and an eighths fraction as whole numbers, which is an LCM of 25 and 8.

q22a tagged areas_of_triangles before trigonometry_missing_sides even though three of the six marks are the central angle and the trig for the apothem. The target is the area, and both skills are Shape and Space so the topic column is unaffected.
q11a and q11b tagged equations_and_identities, the node added 2026-09-04 that closed exactly this gap.
q4 (currency conversion) tagged proportion, the documented handling.

q5b ('write 400 m as a fraction of 2 km') tagged simplifying_fractions then converting_measurements: two of the three marks are the simplified fraction, one the unit conversion. Forming a fraction from a context remains a documented gap and simplifying is the nearest honest node.
